sections.html:
You'll find both the Assessor and the Collector in the courthouse complex at 411 Jules Street, St. Joseph. Room 123 is the Collector (816-271-1401, fax 816-271-1584). Rooms 122 and 222 are the Assessor (816-271-1520). Weekday hours at both are 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM.

About $100 million in tax revenue moves through the Collector every year on its way to 33 taxing districts. Besides printing statements, the office issues Merchant and Manufacturer licenses and conducts the August delinquent tax sale. The Assessor, an elected official, maintains a roll of more than 40,000 real parcels and over 110,000 articles of personal property.

St. Joseph, the seat, had 72,473 residents in 2020, and the county runs along the Missouri River in Missouri's northwest corner. The county has lost people: 89,201 in 2010, an estimated 83,540 in 2025. Schools come from the St. Joseph district plus Buchanan County R-IV (De Kalb), East Buchanan County C-1 (Gower), Mid-Buchanan County R-V (Faucett) and North Platte County R-I.

  • 38,615 housing units in 2025
  • 66.3 percent of homes owner-occupied, 2020-2024
  • $166,300 typical value for an owner-occupied home
  • $902 median gross rent
  • 52 building permits in 2025

By about July 1 the Assessor completes the roll and hands it to the County Clerk. Districts set budgets and levies near the end of September, and the Assessor plays no role in that step.

sections.h2: Payment due date and ways to pay
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in the first week of November. The Collector wants payment when you receive yours, and December 31 divides on time from late. To count, a payment must arrive by that date or bear an official U.S. Postal Service postmark. Metered postage from a private machine doesn't qualify. State law on mailed payments is in RSMo 139.100.

Nothing in the mailbox by the end of November? Ask the office for a copy, because a missing bill doesn't waive interest or penalties. Online payers get a mailed receipt in three to five business days, so pay in person if you need one within seven. Accepted: cash, check, American Express, Discover, MasterCard and Visa. Phone payments aren't taken, and replacing a lost receipt costs $1.

sections.h2: If Buchanan County taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
The Collector applies money to old debt first. Delinquent real estate and personal property tax must be cleared before any payment counts toward the current year. After December 31, use the payment schedule printed on the statement.

Once land is in the back tax book, RSMo 140.100 adds a penalty of 18 percent of that year's delinquency, or no more than 2 percent a month if the owner redeems ahead of the sale. Under RSMo 140.150, delinquent land can be sold on the fourth Monday of August. Beforehand the Collector must send the recorded owner a first class letter, plus a certified one if assessed value exceeds $1,000. Until the sale, you may pay the tax, penalty and costs and keep the property.

The county's website points to two programs. First, the state Property Tax Credit returns up to $750 to residents who are 65 or older, totally disabled or disabled by military service, or who are 60 or older and draw surviving spouse Social Security. Income, counting Social Security, must stay at or under $25,000 for one filer and $27,000 for a married couple. Call 573-751-3505 at the Department of Revenue, or 800-877-6881 to get Form MO-PTC.

Second, in September 2024 the County Commission opted into the Senior Citizen Homestead Property Tax Credit (RSMo 137.1050). Homeowners 62 and older can lock the bill on a primary residence at the level of their qualifying year. That caps future increases and pays nothing back. Ask the courthouse when the next application window opens.

sections.h2: Taxes and recording when you sell
sections.html:
Selling doesn't cancel the year's bill, so agree on who pays what before closing. Get the parcel's balance from the Collector, keeping in mind that old taxes clear first. Name, mailing address and legal description issues go to the Assessor instead.

The Recorder of Deeds is in Room 103 of the same building at 411 Jules Street, phone 816-271-1437. Nothing is recorded after 4:00 PM. Documents delivered later are filed in the order received at 8:00 AM the next business day, a real concern if a closing drags near December 31 or a payoff deadline. The Recorder can't draft a deed or give legal advice, so lean on a title company or attorney.

A cash buyer removes the lender payoff from the timeline. The tax balance and the 4:00 PM recording cutoff still apply, so schedule signing in the morning when you can.

sections.h2: Preparing a Buchanan County house for sale
sections.html:
Most tax trouble at a closing can be spotted weeks ahead. Work through this list once you decide to sell.

  1. Call 816-271-1401 and ask the Collector for the balance on your parcel, including any older year.
  2. Check the statement for the right name, mailing address and legal description. If something is off, the Assessor at 816-271-1520 fixes it.
  3. Ask whether you have a senior credit or freeze that will end when the house sells, so the buyer knows what to expect on their own bill.
  4. Tell the title company about any payment you made online, since the mailed receipt takes three to five business days.
  5. Plan the signing so the deed reaches the Recorder before 4:00 PM.

If a statement hasn't come by the end of November, don't wait. Ask for a copy, because the December 31 deadline and its penalties still apply to the owner of record.

The Assessor's office is the place to ask how your value was reached. Not satisfied? File with the Board of Equalization by the second Monday in July. After the board rules you have 30 days to go to the State Tax Commission, a right set out in RSMo 138.430.

Pay without protest and skip both appeals, and that year's assessment is final, though next year's can be challenged. An LLC, trust, estate or corporation needs an attorney to appeal to the State Tax Commission. Bring comparable sales or an appraisal to any hearing.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Buchanan County property tax?
faqs.a: December 31. It has to reach the Collector or bear an official USPS postmark by then. A private postage meter mark doesn't count.

faqs.q: Where is the Buchanan County Collector located?
faqs.a: In Room 123 at 411 Jules Street, St. Joseph, open weekdays 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Call 816-271-1401.

faqs.q: Can I pay Buchanan County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes, using the county's Pay/View Taxes application. It adds a convenience fee that the Collector neither sets nor keeps. For a receipt in under seven days, pay in person.

faqs.q: When is the Buchanan County tax sale?
faqs.a: Each August. State law sets delinquent land sales for the fourth Monday of the month.

faqs.q: Is there a senior tax freeze in Buchanan County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county adopted the Senior Citizen Homestead Property Tax Credit in September 2024 for owners 62 and over. It holds a primary residence's bill steady and pays no refund.
